'''''Cercidiphyllum japonicum''''', known as the '''Katsura''' (from its Japanese name カツラ, 桂), is a species of flowering tree in the family [[Cercidiphyllaceae]] native to [[China]] and [[Japan]]. It is sometimes called ''caramel tree'' for the light [[caramel]] smell it emits during leaf fall.<ref>[http://h2g2.com/edited_entry/A87790026 Katsura - the Caramel tree]. In ''h2g2.com''.</ref> It is also sometimes called ''candyfloss tree'' because of the scent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=How to Grow Katsura Tree {{!}} BBC Gardeners World Magazine |url=https://www.gardenersworld.com/how-to/grow-plants/how-to-grow-katsura-tree/ |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=www.gardenersworld.com |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Description==
The tree is [[deciduous]] and grows to 10–45 meters tall, with a trunk diameter of up to 2 meters (rarely more).<ref name=andrews>Andrews, S. (1998, 1999). Tree of the Year: ''Cercidiphyllum japonicum''. ''International Dendrology Society Yearbook'' 1997: 17-45; 1998: 33-38.</ref><ref name=foc>Flora of China: [http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200007098 ''Cercidiphyllum japonicum'']</ref><ref name=chen>Chen, C., Liu, Y-H., Fu, C-X., & Qiu, Y-X. (2010). New microsatellite markers for the rare plant ''Cercidiphyllum japonicum'' and their utility for ''Cercidiphyllum magnificum''. ''Amer. J. Bot''. 97 (9): e82–e84 {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130223144736/http://www.amjbot.org/content/97/9/e82.full.pdf+html|title=full text}}.</ref>

[[File:Cercidiphyllum japonicum JPG01b.jpg|left|thumb|Closeup of leaves, showing seasonal coloration]]
The shoots are dimorphic, with long shoots forming the structure of the branches and short shoots being born from their second year onward. The leaves are produced in opposite pairs on long shoots and singly on short shoots; they have a 1.4–4.7 cm petiole, and are rounded with a heart-shaped base and a crenate margin. Leaves on short shoots are larger, 3.7–9 cm long and 5–8.3 cm broad, and those on long shoots smaller, being 3.2–4.5 cm long and 1.9–3.2 cm broad. The leaves turn a variety of pinks and yellows in autumn and sometimes have a distinctive [[caramel]] scent when in fresh autumn colors. The flowers are inconspicuous and produced in early spring among the opening leaves, with male and female flowers on separate plants ([[Dioecy|dioecious]]). The fruit is a cluster of two to four [[follicle (fruit)|follicles]] 1–1.8 cm long and 2–3 mm wide with each follicle containing several winged seeds.<ref name=andrews/><ref name=foc/>

==Status==
[[File:Cercidiphyllum japonicum2.jpg|thumb|''A Cercidiphyllum japonicum'' branch with fruit.]]
The species is listed as [[Endangered species|endangered]] in China, but overall when Japanese populations are included ''C. japonicum'' is classified as being lower risk.<ref name=chen/> The Chinese populations were sometimes distinguished in the past as ''Cercidiphyllum japonicum'' var. ''sinense'' Rehder & E.H.Wilson, but this is now generally regarded as not distinct from the species.<ref name=andrews/><ref name=foc/>

==Cultivation==
[[File:Cercidiphyllum japonicum502.jpg|thumb|upright|A katsura plank]]
Katsura is a popular ornamental tree in Japan as well as elsewhere. In Japan, it is also grown for its timber, which is used for construction and woodworking.

Several different [[cultivar]]s are grown, including 'Aureum', 'Heronswood Globe', and 'Ruby'.
